title: Khami Ruins
summary: Khami, west of Bulawayo in Zimbabwe, was the capital of the Torwa dynasty that arose after the collapse of the Great Zimbabwe Kingdom. UNESCO dates it 1450-1650 and says it was abandoned during Ndebele incursions in the 19th century. Chirikure describes dry-stone terraces forming platforms for buildings. UNESCO says finds of European and Chinese objects show it was a major trade centre.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO: Torwa dynasty between 1450-1650; Chirikure: flourished between ad 1450 and 1650. UNESCO says abandonment came in the 19th century.

as_recorded.value: capital of the Torwa dynasty, which arose from the collapse of the Great Zimbabwe Kingdom between 1450 -1650

where.modern_name: Khami Ruins National Monument, Matabeleland North, Zimbabwe
where.historical_name: Khami, capital of the Torwa dynasty

importance.justification: UNESCO calls it a unique and exceptional testimony to a civilization which has disappeared and evidence for the chronological development of the Zimbabwe tradition.

reviewer_note: No model: no height was found. UNESCO gives the area as about 108 ha over about 2 km, Chirikure at least 120 ha; neither is used. Chirikure says power later passed violently to Danamombe and puts Khami about twenty kilometres south-west of Bulawayo; UNESCO says abandonment came during 19th-century Ndebele incursions. The Chirikure PDF was downloaded from ORA and read; the URL given is the ORA record. Chirikure also writes Khami as ad 1450-1820 in one passage; the record uses his and UNESCO's 1450-1650.
